_description: Joint-grounding eval for the companion-merge augment_companion default-ON decision (ADR-0018 B4, spec §12). Each ANS query targets a fact that lives in ONE modality (lecture TRANSCRIPT or its SLIDE DECK) and is genuinely absent from / sparse in the aligned counterpart — so the win for `companion_augment_enabled` is a refuse/miss→answer flip when augment pulls the reranked winner's aligned counterpart. The 6 CR350 transcript↔deck pairs are linked in the vault (companion_alignments.json). Candidates discovered + verified 2026-06-14.
_purpose: Measure whether augment ON produces an answer/recall WIN over OFF (decision: default-ON iff a clean measured win + refusal_cf=1.0; else measured-defer to default-OFF opt-in).
_note: Run augment-OFF (baseline) vs augment-ON (MEMEX_AGENTS__COMPANION_AUGMENT_ENABLED=true) and compare answered_count + mean_answer_mention_recall. relevant_chunk_ids intentionally omitted (cp is not the metric here).

_baseline_2026_06_14.ab: companion_augment_enabled OFF (baseline) vs ON (MEMEX_AGENTS__COMPANION_AUGMENT_ENABLED=true), N=2 each, over the 6 linked CR350 transcript↔deck pairs (companion_alignments.json).
_baseline_2026_06_14.result: DOUBLE-EDGED, NET-ZERO. answered 8/15 BOTH OFF and ON; refusal_cf=1.0 both; mean_answer_mention_recall 1.0 both (answered subset). Two DETERMINISTIC per-query flips CANCEL: -03 (MAC/OUI) refuse→correct = a genuine joint-grounding WIN (the deck ARP slide wins retrieval, augment pulls the transcript OUI commentary) BUT -09 (rate-limiting threshold) correct→REFUSE = a CROWDING regression (augment's appended counterparts tipped the assess/answer gate to over-refuse a query whose answer '100 requests/second' was STILL present in the chunks). Mechanism fired (13 augment_companion.added events/run ON, 0 OFF).
_baseline_2026_06_14.decision: MEASURED-DEFER → companion_augment_enabled stays DEFAULT-OFF (opt-in). No clean win (net-zero) + a real crowding regression; the decision rule (~3-4 clean flips, no degradation) is NOT met. The CR350 modalities are too REDUNDANT (the teacher elaborates the slides, but the answer is usually in the directly-retrieved modality) for augment to net-win, and additive-to-reranked appends dilute borderline queries (the expand_graph / usage_intent_demotion precedent). HARD-gate-safe (refusal_cf=1.0 — no hallucination). REVISIT IF: a less-redundant transcript/deck corpus appears OR the crowding regression is fixed (insert counterparts adjacent to their winner / a crowding-resistant assess) — a future lever, NOT built.
_baseline_2026_06_14.compete_experiment_2026_06_14: The crowding fix was TESTED: a COMPETE variant (re-rank window+counterparts, keep the window SIZE so counterparts compete instead of unconditionally appending) A/B'd N=2 → scored IDENTICAL to OFF on EVERY query (-03 win vanished WITH -09 regression). Structural reason: a companion counterpart is aligned-by-companion, not retrieved, so it can't out-rank the already-best top-k → always cut → augment becomes a no-op; the -03 win existed ONLY via append's UNCONDITIONAL entry. → the win and the crowding regression are INSEPARABLE; NO code fix exists (counterpart-adjacent insertion changes order not the set; re-rank neuters). Code reverted. Revisit ONLY with a genuinely less-redundant corpus (a curator/data question).
